description: SGLang serving RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (+ DSpark draft) on desg0 (single engine, scraped at desg0:8000, job "sglang"). Engine limits it is read against (set in hosts/desg0/sglang_qwen3_container.nix): --max-running-requests 4, --context-length 131072, --mem-fraction-static 0.62, fp8 KV cache, bf16 mamba (GDN) SSM state, DSpark speculative decoding. SGLang exposes /metrics only when started with --enable-metrics (default OFF; set in the container config). All rates and histogram quantiles use the shared rate window via the "Rate window" variable (5m default, 30m option); means are rate(_sum)/rate(_count), restart-safe. Metric names are `sglang:*` (the `vllm:*` series ended when the engine was swapped, 2026-07). SGLang's /metrics registry carries no process_* / python_* series, so the former uptime/RSS/CPU panels are gone. SGLang also has no finished-reason label on completed requests (aborts are separate: sglang:num_aborted_requests_total).
title: sglang

panels.description: Completed requests per hour over the selected rate window. sglang:num_requests_total counts finished requests; aborted ones never reach it and are shown in "Requests / h by mode".
panels.title: Requests / h

panels.description: Output (generation) tokens per second across all streams, smoothed over the selected rate window. The headline serving throughput.
panels.title: Generation tok/s

panels.description: Requests currently in model execution batches. Hard cap is --max-running-requests 4; sitting at 4 with a non-empty queue means the engine is saturated.
panels.title: Running requests (max 4)

panels.description: Requests queued for scheduling. Anything sustained above 0 means clients are paying queue time; see Queue time p95 in the Scheduler row.
panels.title: Waiting requests

panels.description: KV token-pool utilization (1 = full). Sized by --mem-fraction-static 0.62 with fp8 KV; long agent contexts (up to 131072 tokens) eat it fast. Sustained ~1 causes queueing and retractions.
panels.title: KV cache usage

panels.description: p95 time to first token over the selected rate window. Dominated by prefill of long agent prompts plus queue time; this is what makes an agent feel slow to start.
panels.title: TTFT p95

panels.description: Time to first token: how long a client waits before the stream starts. = queue time + prefill. Histogram buckets top out at 400s, so quantiles are trustworthy across the whole expected range.
panels.title: Time to first token

panels.description: Inter-token latency: the gap between consecutive tokens of one stream, i.e. perceived typing speed (1 / ITL = tokens/s per client). Buckets top out at 8s; with DSpark speculative decoding the effective ITL is per verified batch, so this is smoother than vllm's was.
panels.title: Inter-token latency

panels.description: End-to-end request latency (arrival to last token). For long agent generations this is mostly decode time, so it tracks output length rather than engine health -- compare with the per-stage breakdown to the right. Buckets top out at 2400s.
panels.title: End-to-end request latency

panels.description: Mean seconds a request spends in each observed stage over the selected rate window (stage label: tokenize, request_process, prefill_forward, chunked_prefill, spec_draft, spec_verify, ...). Queue time is not a stage here -- see Queue time p95 in the Scheduler row.
panels.title: Mean time per request stage

panels.description: Prompt (prefill) vs generation (decode) tokens per second, smoothed over the selected rate window. Prompt spikes mark new agent conversations; with the radix cache, warm turns mostly re-use cached prefix (see Caching row).
panels.title: Token rate

panels.description: Completed requests per hour by streaming mode, plus aborts/h. SGLang does not label finished requests with a reason (vllm's finished_reason is gone); aborts (client disconnected / 4xx mid-stream) are the only failure signal and count separately.
panels.title: Requests / h by mode + aborts

panels.description: HTTP responses per hour by endpoint and status code (sglang:http_responses_total, the SGLang ASGI-middleware counterpart of vllm's http_requests_total). 4xx on /v1/chat/completions usually means a client sent something the server rejects (e.g. a prompt over --context-length); 5xx means the engine broke. Rejected requests never reach sglang:num_requests_total, so this is the only place they show up.
panels.title: HTTP responses / h by endpoint & status

panels.description: Engine-side generation throughput gauge (per scheduler), versus the request-side token rate panel to the left: they should track each other. Dips below the request-side rate indicate retracted/stalled decode work.
panels.title: Generation throughput (engine gauge)

panels.description: Retractions in the last 24h -- SGLang's equivalent of vllm preemptions. A retraction evicts a running request's KV (or mamba state) to make room for others and re-runs it; the clearest sign the pools are too small for the offered load (raise --max-running-requests together with --max-mamba-cache-size, or the memory fraction).
panels.title: Retractions (24h)

panels.description: p95 time requests spent in the WAITING phase over the selected rate window. Non-trivial values mean requests are being admitted late, not served slowly.
panels.title: Queue time p95

panels.description: Rejected/failed HTTP responses per hour (4xx + 5xx, all endpoints), smoothed over the selected rate window. Any sustained value means a client is misconfigured or the engine is erroring; break it down in the HTTP panel above.
panels.title: HTTP 4xx+5xx / h

panels.description: Output tokens per second as a single client experiences it (1 / mean inter-token latency). Independent of how many requests are in flight, unlike the aggregate generation tok/s.
panels.title: Per-stream tok/s

panels.description: KV token-pool utilization over time. Sawtooth = normal scheduling; a plateau near 1 together with waiting requests or retractions means the KV cache is the binding constraint. The GPU is shared with llama.cpp, so the ceiling cannot simply be raised.
panels.title: KV cache usage

panels.description: Mamba (GDN) SSM state-pool utilization -- the hybrid-architecture twin of the KV pool. Pinned by --max-mamba-cache-size 16 (= 4 requests x S=4 extra_buffer_lazy slots); the pool saturates at max-running-requests, not at context length. Sustained ~1 means a mamba retraction is one more request away.
panels.title: Mamba (GDN) state usage

panels.description: Scheduler occupancy: running requests (capped at --max-running-requests 4) against the admission queue. running pinned at 4 with waiting > 0 = the engine is saturated for the offered load.
panels.title: Running vs waiting requests

panels.description: KV token-pool occupancy in absolute tokens: used = actively referenced by running requests, evictable = radix-cached (re-usable by the prefix cache), available = free. Pool size ~445052 tokens (see Engine config row).
panels.title: KV token pool

panels.description: Prompt tokens per request. Explains prefill cost and TTFT. The default histogram buckets reach ~1.1M tokens, so quantiles stay trustworthy well beyond the 131072 context limit (vllm's saturated at 50k).
panels.title: Prompt tokens per request

panels.description: Generation tokens per request. When it plateaus at the max_tokens clients asked for, answers are being truncated -- cross-check the HTTP panel and client configs.
panels.title: Generation tokens per request

panels.description: Mean acceptance length per verify step: accepted draft tokens + the bonus token. The verify window is gamma+1 = 8 slots, so 8 = every draft accepted; a sustained drop means the draft model is losing agreement with the target (e.g. on out-of-distribution inputs) and decode pays full-length verify cost.
panels.title: Spec accept length (max 8)

panels.description: Speculative acceptance rate (accepted drafts / proposed drafts per batch, 1 = perfect agreement). Track it next to the accept length: the length says how much work each verify saves, the rate says how reliable the draft model is.
panels.title: Spec accept rate

panels.description: Radix-cache hit rate as reported by the scheduler (cached query tokens / queried tokens). Unlike vllm -- where prefix caching was hard-disabled for this hybrid GDN architecture and the series stayed at 0 -- SGLang's mamba-radix-cache (extra_buffer_lazy) can serve prompt prefixes from cache, so a non-trivial ratio here is expected on warm agent conversations.
panels.title: Radix cache hit rate

panels.description: Prompt tokens per second served from the radix cache versus freshly computed. The cached side saves prefill compute and TTFT on warm turns; if cache tokens collapse to 0 while traffic continues, eviction is outpacing the workload (see KV token pool).
panels.title: Cached vs fresh prompt tokens / s

panels.description: Scrape health of desg0:8000. 0/no data means the container is down, restarting (model load takes minutes), or --enable-metrics got dropped -- check `systemctl status podman-sglang-qwen3` on desg0.
panels.title: Target up

panels.description: GPU memory split at startup, reported by the engine: NVFP4 weights, fp8 KV pool, and CUDA-graph buffers. They should sum to roughly --mem-fraction-static 0.62 of the 96GB card (the rest is shared with llama.cpp). SGLang's /metrics carries no process_* series, so the former API-server RSS/CPU panels are gone.
panels.title: GPU memory pools

panels.description: Engine configuration constants as emitted at startup: the advertised context length (--context-length 131072) and the total KV token pool (~445k at the current mem-fraction). A reset to 0/blank between up periods is a restart; the series is constant between restarts.
panels.title: Context length & KV pool size
